title: A pilot study to investigate the immunological regulation of preeclampsia
summary:
Around 2 % of pregnancies in Europe are affected by preeclampsia. And despite being responsible for 20-25 % of perinatal deaths and 10-15 % of maternal deaths, the cause of preeclampsia is still unknown. Preeclampsia is a placenta-dependent hypertensive disorder which is defined by gestational hypertension and proteinuria after finished 20. pregnancy week. Every patient need to me monitored continiously and in many cases treatment in hospital is neccessary. The only therapy option is premature termination of the pregnancy. So you need to balance the health of mother against child before therapy. 
Next to genetic factors and maternal/environmental factors, a maladaption of the maternal immune system is discussed as a cause of preeclampsia. We want to concentrate on that aspect and investigate the immunological regulation of preeclampsia. When discussing the immune system causing preeclampsia, one assumes that the maternal-fetal immune tolerance went wrong and leading to an immune reaction against the fetus. This hypothesis is supported by all immunological symptoms of preeclampsia. We have inflammatory cells and conditions in preeclampsia, compared to a normal pregancy. 
So we want to know what triggers this immune reaction and which marker for an earlier diagnosis and prognosis marker can be extrapolated from that. In general you can observe that nearly all symptoms of preeclampsia are strongly controlled immunologically. Thats why we are convinced that the immune regulation of preeclampsia is a good starting point to find marker for an earlier diagnosis, prognosis marker and a future therapy of preeclampsia. For that we will take up several research hypotheses and plan a broad approach thematically and methodically. We hope for a better characterization of the disease and more knowledge about the clinical course.
